key_insight: ViTamyloid is a two-stage AI pipeline that segments and classifies amyloid-β lesions in brain histology, enabling much more detailed lesion-level quantification than manual scoring.
clinical_relevance: This could improve neuropathology research and AD staging by turning heterogeneous amyloid pathology into scalable, reproducible measurements across whole-slide images.
method: Stage 1: EfficientNet B4 + U-Net with Faster R-CNN to segment amyloid-positive regions and separate confluent lesions.
Stage 2: Frozen UNI2-h pathology foundation model plus a trainable ViT Adapter to classify lesion candidates into five amyloid categories.
Tested across donor-disjoint splits and independent datasets with different antibodies, scanners, resolutions, and image quality.
evidence_signal: In donor-disjoint evaluation, the model achieved macro F1 0.903, with high AUPRC/AUROC across lesion classes and better performance than frozen features alone and published comparison pipelines.
watch_item: Performance was shown on digital pathology datasets, so real-world deployment will still need external validation, stain/scanner harmonization, and pathologist oversight.
paper_title: Generalizing Amyloid β Pathology from Postmortem Human Brains with Vision Foundation Models for Lesion Quantification
